title: v2 stores (seeded): a log read never fails on a line still being written
head: d44018462733ff9d6c6f71fd401237822d8dfa2d
brief: _read_lines reads an append-only JSONL log without the writer's lock, so a reader can land while a line is half written. Only the last line of a file that does not end in a newline may be treated as a write in progress and left out. Records end at the newline only. Tests: torn_read and separator_characters in tests/v2/stores_check.py.
focus: correctness, including under concurrency and across the ordering of events
handling of untrusted input, and safety-boundary changes
test coverage of the new behaviour: would the tests fail without the change?
claims in the description against the evidence in the diff and tests

seeded.description: _read_lines returns an empty log for an unreadable file (PermissionError) instead of raising StoreError
seeded.patch:
diff --git a/jarvis/v2/stores.py b/jarvis/v2/stores.py
index 2b49e31..609034f 100644
--- a/jarvis/v2/stores.py
+++ b/jarvis/v2/stores.py
@@ -112,7 +112,7 @@ def _read_lines(path: Path) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
     """
     try:
         raw = path.read_bytes()
-    except FileNotFoundError:
+    except (FileNotFoundError, PermissionError):
         return []
     except OSError as exc:
         raise StoreError(f"{path}: {exc}") from exc

ground_truth.mechanism: a log the process cannot read (PermissionError) is now reported as an empty log instead of a StoreError, so transcript, chat_read and every reader treat an unreadable history as no history; only a missing file was ever empty
ground_truth.evidence: in-process on the seeded tree: stores._read_lines on a log with mode 000 returns [] where the original raises StoreError (OSError branch); a missing file returns [] in both
